q1: SELECT ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID FROM ACTORDIRECTOR GROUP BY ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID HAVING COUNT(*)>=3
q2: SELECT D1.ACTOR_ID, D1.DIRECTOR_ID FROM ACTORDIRECTOR D1 GROUP BY ACTOR_ID, DIRECTOR_ID HAVING COUNT(DIRECTOR_ID) >=3
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID FROM ACTORDIRECTOR GROUP BY ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID HAVING COUNT(*)>=3
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT D1.ACTOR_ID, D1.DIRECTOR_ID FROM ACTORDIRECTOR D1 GROUP BY ACTOR_ID, DIRECTOR_ID HAVING COUNT(DIRECTOR_ID) >=3
counterexample: INSERT INTO ACTORDIRECTOR (TIMESTAMP, ACTOR_ID, DIRECTOR_ID) VALUES (1, 1, 1), (2, 1, 2), (3, 1, 1), (4, 1, 3), (5, 1, 2), (6, 1, 1);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because Q1 groups by both ACTOR_ID and DIRECTOR_ID, while Q2 groups by ACTOR_ID and uses COUNT(DIRECTOR_ID) in the HAVING clause. This can lead to different results if there are multiple rows with the same ACTOR_ID and different DIRECTOR_IDs.
counterexample_dsp: A test case where an actor has worked with the same director multiple times, but with different directors as well, leading to different results between Q1 and Q2.
